title: Standard and Bipolar Rectification in Tilted Periodically-Driven Quantum Systems
abstract: Developing mechanisms to control transport in correlated quantum systems is essential for advancing quantum circuit technologies. In this work, we establish a rectification mechanism for both particle and energy flow in a fermionic system coupled to external baths, in the presence of a tilted potential modulated locally by a time-periodic drive. The drive generates particle and energy currents even in the absence of chemical or thermal bias between the baths. These drive-induced currents are enhanced at resonant frequencies at which avoided crossings occur in the Floquet quasienergy spectrum, reflecting the role of the Floquet states as intermediate channels for transport. Once a bias between the baths is introduced, the drive-induced current contribution can reinforce, compete with, or even cancel the bias-induced contribution. These effects enable rectification in the non-interacting regime, which we quantify via the rectification coefficient $\mathcal{R}$. This coefficient measures the asymmetry between transport up the tilt (forward bias) and down the tilt (reverse bias). In addition to standard rectification, where transport is reduced under reverse bias, we identify a regime of bipolar rectification, in which the current flows only up the tilt regardless of the bias polarity. At the boundary between standard and bipolar regimes, the system achieves perfect rectification, corresponding to complete suppression of the reverse-bias current. In the presence of interactions between particles, the parameter region that supports bipolar rectification is enlarged and $\mathcal{R}$ can be enhanced by many orders of magnitude. Our results establish a rectification mechanism for particle and energy transport that can be experimentally realized in condensed matter and cold atom systems.
summary: This paper details a mechanism to control quantum transport in driven fermionic systems by inducing particle and energy currents even without external bias. It quantifies this control using a rectification coefficient, identifying a unique 'bipolar rectification' regime. The findings demonstrate that interactions can significantly enhance this effect, offering a pathway for realizing quantum diodes in solid-state or cold atom platforms.
main_problem: The work aims to develop mechanisms to control particle and energy transport in correlated quantum systems, which is crucial for advancing quantum circuit technologies.
main_result: The authors establish a mechanism for both particle and energy rectification, identifying a novel regime called bipolar rectification where current flows only in one direction regardless of the bias polarity.
method: The analysis quantifies transport using the rectification coefficient ($\mathcal{R}$) by comparing drive-induced and bias-induced currents, analyzing the system's response in non-equilibrium steady states.
model_or_system: The model is a fermionic system coupled to external baths, subjected to a tilted potential modulated locally by a time-periodic drive. The Hamiltonian includes terms for the system, the baths, and the coupling.
key_observables: Rectification coefficient ($\mathcal{R}$), particle current ($J_P$), energy current ($J_E$), and the contrast coefficient ($C$).
important_parameters: The driving frequency ($\omega$), the strength of interactions ($U$), and the presence/absence of chemical or thermal bias.
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed using a mesoscopic leads approach and is shown to operate even in the non-interacting regime, though interactions enhance the effect.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the mechanism, showing how drive-induced currents peak at avoided crossings in the Floquet spectrum, and how the contrast coefficient ($C$) transitions between standard and bipolar rectification regimes.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general mechanism for drive-induced currents in the presence of a tilt. It then analyzes the competition between drive-induced and bias-induced currents to define the rectification coefficient and identify the bipolar regime. Finally, it extends the analysis to include particle interactions, showing enhancement of the effect.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium transport and rectification in periodically driven systems, which is a major focus area in modern AMO physics and quantum thermodynamics. The identification of bipolar rectification is a novel, controllable transport feature.
